newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin on schedule for heart surgery - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin on schedule for heart surgery - Kremlin.

text.p: The Kremlin, denying reports that President Boris Yeltsin's planned heart operation was likely to be delayed, said on Tuesday that preparations for surgery were going according to schedule.

"Nobody anywhere has talked about a change in plans for the period either before or after the operation," press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference. "Everything is going according to plan, to the full extent."
Virtually non-stop rumours about Yeltsin's health have clearly annoyed the Kremlin, which is forced to deny them to calm nervous financial markets.

The latest report, on the Moscow-based Ekho Moskvy radio station, quoted sources at the Central Clinical Hospital as saying Yeltsin's haemoglobin levels were so low that few surgeons would recommend an operation in the foreseeable future.
Haemoglobin is the colouring that produces the red colour of blood and plays a key role in carrying oxygen around the body.
Some Russian shares edged lower on Tuesday.
But Yastrzhembsky said tests showed that the quality of Yeltsin's blood had improved in the last week.
"Preparations for the operation are going according to plan," he said.
Yeltsin, 65, had two heart attacks last year and doctors have said they will operate within two months to improve the blood supply to his heart.
But they admitted last month that inexplicably low haemoglobin levels were a problem and said more tests were needed to work out what was wrong.
After the operation the president will spend some weeks convalescing, but doctors have said there is no reason why he cannot return to a normal, active life.

Yeltsin has rarely been seen in public since he was reelected for a second term on July 3. After a spell in hospital he is now at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow where he met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and the president of Turkmenistan on Tuesday.
